messages.author: f66907f526d3c7bf
messages.subject: INLA getting totally wrong answer with simple Poison model
parts:
Now, this is worrying. I'm starting an analysis of some abundance data, and INLA is giving weird results. The counts are all fairly high, but nothing excessive. But even with just an intercept in the model, INLA estimates hte intercept as about 50, whereas it should be about 6.3 (on the log scale, of course).

I'm using INLA v0.0-1452148058 on R version 3.2.2 (2015-08-14) -- "Fire Safety" running on x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (64-bit).

The data and code are below, followed by the output from the models.

Help?

Bob


library(INLA)
Counts <- structure(list(Counts = c(657L, 589L, 516L, 563L, 668L, 708L,
                          796L, 601L, 677L, 522L, 564L, 597L, 527L, 555L, 529L, 578L, 496L,
                          429L, 516L, 522L, 577L, 546L, 410L, 510L, 420L, 449L, 397L, 390L,
                          372L, 417L, 418L, 358L, 348L, 289L, 356L, 356L, 361L, 378L, 378L,
                          426L, 381L, 409L, 387L, 488L, 526L, 577L, 582L, 475L, 493L, 419L,
                          296L, 422L, 363L, 378L, 389L, 423L, 466L, 460L, 475L, 469L, 490L,
                          478L, 448L, 474L, 482L, 474L, 377L, 421L, 384L, 435L, 495L, 545L,
                          636L, 543L, 581L, 623L, 523L, 595L, 620L, 583L, 613L, 661L, 656L,
                          597L, 661L, 717L, 587L, 472L, 478L, 455L, 406L, 439L, 451L, 445L,
                          290L, 366L, 367L, 356L, 410L, 685L, 698L, 908L, 1154L, 1151L,
                          952L, 953L, 941L, 840L, 876L, 679L, 590L, 546L, 676L, 630L, 570L,
                          422L, 465L, 340L, 308L, 399L)), .Names = "Counts")


glm.res <- summary(glm(Counts ~ 1, family="poisson",data=Counts))
inla.res <- summary(inla(Counts ~ 1, family="poisson",data=Counts))

messages.subject: Updating INLA on Windows, Was: [r-inla] INLA getting totally wrong answer with simple Poison model
parts:
A quick Google search claims that on MS/Windows, packages that are loaded in memory cannot be updated. However, if that's the case I would have expected others to have had the same problem already. But try the workaround of making a fresh INLA installation instead of running the update command.
